title: Hybrid Edge Access Forensics Runbook
author: Sofia Patel
content:
Summary:
This runbook defines the evidence collection, chain-of-custody, and investigation workflow for incidents that affect hybrid and edge model deployments (VPC, on-prem appliances, and cloud-edge nodes). It integrates RBAC and authentication validation, audit logging extraction, data residency constraints, and secure-SDLC gates for incident-driven rollbacks and evidence production. The procedures below are intended for oncall engineers, SREs, and incident response (IR) teams working with security and legal.

Overview:

Purpose:
- Provide a repeatable, compliance-ready process to gather, preserve, and analyze evidence from hybrid/edge inference nodes after a security incident.
- Ensure evidence is collected in a way that preserves data residency requirements and audit trail integrity.

Scope:
- Applies to Redwood Inference private deployments (VPC and on-prem), hybrid-edge nodes (cloud-edge appliances), and associated control-plane services.
- Covers incidents that may involve unauthorized access, entitlements misuse, model exfiltration, or anomalous inference traffic.

Key principles:
- Minimal-impact collection: prioritize volatile evidence capture before performing intrusive actions that could destroy forensic artifacts.
- Legal & residency-aware packaging: enforce data locality constraints when packaging evidence (e.g., store EU-region artifacts in EU-resident S3 buckets).
- RBAC-first triage: rapidly validate entitlement scope of affected principals and preserve authorization logs.
- Immutable provenance: tag all artifacts with cryptographic hashes and signed manifests for audit evidence.

Ownership & Roles:
- Incident Commander (IC): named oncall SRE or security incident lead (Duty: coordinate collection and legal hold).
- Forensic Lead: security engineer with forensics experience (Duty: run evidence commands, produce manifest).
- Platform Owner: owner of the affected deployment (Duty: provide access, environment context).
- Legal & Compliance: engage for cross-border evidence guidance and legal hold decisions.
- QA/Product (SDLC gate): advise on rollback or model disablement decisions.

Detection & Triage Checklist (first 30 minutes):
1) Capture incident summary: who/what/where/when (service, node id, tenant id, region).
2) Freeze high-risk automated jobs (e.g., cron inference sweeps) — note as action in incident log.
3) Validate RBAC: run entitlement snapshot for affected principal(s):
   - Command (example): redwood-authz-cli snapshot --principal=svc-data-ingest --out=/tmp/entitlement-snapshot.json
   - Save snapshot to evidence store.
4) Preserve primary audit stream: ensure event-forwarding to the immutable audit collector (if not already):
   - Verify last forwarded sequence numbers and mark window to preserve.
5) Record data residency constraints: list data flows with PII or regulated residency tags (e.g., EU, APAC).

Evidence Priority & Timeline:
- T0-T30 (volatile): process list, network connections, in-memory model cache (KV cache), lua/plugin memory.
- T30-T120 (semi-volatile): container/runtime logs, inference traces, authz decision logs, kernel/driver messages.
- T120+ (persistent): model artifacts, deployment manifests, S3 objects, database rows, long-term audit logs.

Volatile Collection Commands (edge-friendly):
- SSH to node (use bastion or jump host): ssh -J jump.redwood.internal ec2-user@edge-node-12
- Capture process list and open files: sudo /usr/sbin/ss -tunap > /tmp/ss-tcp.log; sudo lsof -nP -p $(pidof runtime) > /tmp/lsof-runtime.log
- Capture GPU/KV cache metadata (if present): sudo /opt/redwood/bin/kv-dump --format=json > /tmp/kv-cache.json
- Memory snapshot (where permitted): sudo gcore -o /tmp/runtime-core $(pidof runtime)  # Require legal approval for export across regions

Audit Log Extraction (minimum required fields):
- Event timestamp (ISO8601), event_id (UUID), principal_id, resource, action, decision (allow/deny), policy_version, request_context (ip, region, node_id), request_id, trace_id.
- Recommended query examples (Splunk/ELK):
  - SPL example: index=redwood_audit action IN ("model.generate","auth.decision") principal_id="svc-*" | sort -_time | table _time,event_id,principal_id,action,decision,request_id,node_id

RBAC & Auth Forensic Snapshot:
- Required artifacts:
  - Entitlement snapshot for each affected principal (user and service).
  - Current role-to-permission mappings and effective policies (policy_version, policy_sha256).
  - SSO/IdP login events and MFA challenges for the timeframe.
- Steps:
  1) Export role bindings: redwood-admin export-roles --format=json > /tmp/roles.json
  2) Export active sessions: redwood-auth export-sessions --filter=node_id=edge-node-12 --out=/tmp/active-sessions.json
  3) Preserve IdP logs via vendor console (Okta/GSuite) and note time-range.

Data Residency & Packaging Rules:
- If any artifact contains PII or is tagged with regional residency (eu, gb, us-ca), store packaged evidence in the corresponding region-specific evidence bucket: s3://redwood-evidence-{region}/incidents/{incident_id}/
- If cross-border transfer is required, obtain Legal approval (document waiver id in manifest) before copying artifacts across regions.
- Retention mapping sample table (documented in manifest):
  - Volatile artifacts: retained for 90 days in staging evidence store, then migrated to long-term with access controls.
  - Immutable audit logs: retained per compliance policy (default: 7 years for regulated customers).

Evidence Manifest (required fields - JSON file):
- incident_id, collector, node_id, region, artifact_list (array of filenames), sha256_hashes (parallel list), legal_hold (true/false), residency_tags, signed_by (forensic lead), signature_timestamp.
- Example (manifest.json snippet):
  {
    "incident_id": "INC-2026-0121-007",
    "collector": "forensic-lead:sofia.patel",
    "node_id": "edge-node-12",
    "region": "eu-west-1",
    "artifact_list": ["/evidence/ss-tcp.log","/evidence/kv-cache.json"],
    "sha256_hashes": ["a3f...", "f12..."],
    "legal_hold": true
  }

Chain-of-Custody & Signing:
1) Each artifact must be hashed (sha256) immediately after collection and before any transfer.
2) Forensic lead uploads artifacts to region bucket with object metadata set: provenance: signed, collector: <email>, original-node: <node_id>, manifest-ref: <manifest_key>.
3) For highly sensitive artifacts, enable server-side encryption with customer-managed keys (CMK) scoped to the residency region.

Analysis & Correlation Guidance:
- Correlate authz decisions with inference traces using trace_id/request_id.
- Map unusual model outputs to input traces (keep prompt snapshots where policy allows).
- Look for patterns: sudden policy-version change, new service principal created, spike of allow decisions for previously-denied resource.

SDLC Integration & Post-Incident Controls:
- If incident is traced to a deployment or release: require an emergency rollback or canary pause via the release gate in the secure SDLC pipeline.
- Release gate checklist for rollback:
  1) Confirm affected revision(s) and the deployment manifest.
  2) Verify canary traffic percentages and health metrics.
  3) Trigger rollback with redwood-deploy rollback --deployment=<id> --to-revision=<rev> and log action in the incident timeline.
  4) Preserve release artifacts (build id, container digest) as evidence.

Risk & Exception Handling:
- If evidence collection cannot be performed in-region due to operational constraints, document an exception using the Entitlement & Residency Exception template and route to Legal for expedited approval.
- Temporary elevated access for forensic collection must be timebound (default 4 hours) and require an approver from security and the platform owner. Record approval in incident ticket.

Evidence Review & Handover to Legal:
- Package assembled evidence with the manifest and signed hashes.
- Provide Legal with a read-only access link to the evidence bucket and a copy of the manifest.
- If evidence is likely to trigger cross-border data transfer concerns, Legal will coordinate data subject notifications and regulatory reporting.

Cleanup & Secure Disposal:
- Schedule evidence lifecycle actions in the manifest. For non-legal-hold artifacts, follow retention and secure deletion policies: shred/overwrite prior to deletion when on-prem storage contains regulated data.
- For cloud-resident evidence: use object-level encryption and then object-delete with retention logs.

Post-incident Actions & Preventive Controls:
- Post-incident review: forensic lead produces a technical appendix summarizing root cause, evidence chain, RBAC changes, and recommended mitigations.
- Required mitigations (examples):
  - Enforce just-in-time privilege activation for admin roles on edge clusters.
  - Harden audit-forwarding with backup collectors per region.
  - Add SDLC release checks for policy changes touching authz rules.

Runbook Appendices:
A. Useful Commands (summary):
- Entitlement snapshot: redwood-authz-cli snapshot --principal=<id> --out=/tmp/entitlement.json
- Export roles: redwood-admin export-roles --format=json > /tmp/roles.json
- Audit query sample (Elastic): POST /_search { "query": { "bool": { "must": [{ "term":{"action":"auth.decision"} }, { "range":{"@timestamp":{"gte":"now-1h"}}}] } } }

B. Evidence Storage Locations (examples):
- EU (evidence): s3://redwood-evidence-eu/incidents/{incident_id}/
- US (evidence): s3://redwood-evidence-us/incidents/{incident_id}/
- On-prem archive: //redwood-archive/evidence/{incident_id}/ (encrypted share)

C. Contacts & Escalation Matrix:
- IC (oncall): oncall-sre@redwood.internal (Pager duty roster)
- Forensic Lead: sofia.patel@redwood.internal
- Legal: incidents-legal@redwood.internal
- Product/Security PM: marcus.liu@redwood.internal

D. Templates & Links:
- Evidence manifest template: /templates/evidence-manifest-v2.json
- Residency exception form: /templates/residency-exception-request.md
- RBAC snapshot policy: /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/entitlement-provenance-and-retention-framework-2026

Revision History:
- 2026-01-12: Draft created by Sofia Patel.
- 2026-03-05: Added RBAC snapshot commands and residency packaging rules (reviewers: Marcus Liu).
- 2026-09-07: Updated manifest schema and legal approval workflow; marked published.

Notes & References:
- This runbook complements existing audit logging and evidence playbooks. Use it when incidents cross hybrid/cloud-edge boundaries or when residency concerns constrain cross-region transfers.
- For any legal questions on cross-border transfer, contact Legal before copying artifacts across regions.

End of document.
